protocol.objectiveChange: Four-times BCE weight within a two-pixel known material boundary band; weights normalized per image before one global A/B assignment. Unknown/background interfaces excluded; half-coverage samples handled symmetrically.
protocol.checkpointSelection: Final update only; no per-photo winners or evaluation-based checkpoint selection.

realTraining.scope: Known partial training labels, not held-out accuracy.

syntheticTraining.scope: All training views; original, printed and scene variants share 32 geometries. Independent raster boundary diagnostic with the same global phase as overall error. Not a topology certificate.

findings: Star, green/silver web and dark/gold checker retain recognizable major structures; small joins and cells remain distorted.
Printed stripes, flowers, letters and trees still become false material boundaries.
Both stacked-heart photographs lose most intended structure; the wide stacked-heart image is nearly a single paper class.
The shaded red/gold checker and green/black motif still lose most of their interiors.
Some red/gold motifs acquire outlines and false islands following shading.
Frozen body errors still exclude house/candlestick regions and include adjacent hands.
Two neighboring-heart scene training views have large whole-region failures despite improved group boundary averages.

conclusion: Boundary weighting improves average synthetic boundary error in all three groups versus the equal-compute uniform control. Printed and clean interiors also improve, while scene interiors and real partial training error regress. The shorter 120-update parent still has lower clean boundary error. Real-photo visual failures prevent integration; no new full template fits or browser export were justified.

supported: More complete sampling/updates alone did not remove material failures.
Changing only boundary weighting improves synthetic edge fit, showing the uniform objective contributes to those errors.
Observed real-photo failures precede corner selection and template fitting: the full-photo material field already erases or invents motif boundaries.
Body-region omissions remain a separate frozen-model limitation.
notEstablished: The exact share of edge error attributable to 160-pixel feature resolution versus model capacity.
Whether RGB calibration from neural seeds repairs the real-photo identity failures.
Generalization to new photographs or improved cutting-template recovery.

next: Diagnose neural material confidence and compare full-resolution RGB mixture calibration from learned paper seeds against unchanged-body RGB clustering. Use a fixed procedure and all same photos; inspect printed and shaded cases separately. Retain boundary weighting as an offline training option, not a release.

validation.applicationScope: Only offline Python tools, experiment plans and reports changed; last application/inverse/build validation remains conni-release-qa.json.
